name: RADAR Adversarial Detection
description: Applies the RADAR (Robust AI-Text Detection via Adversarial Learning) framework. Standard AI detectors are easily defeated by simple paraphrasing tools (like QuillBot) or evasion prompts ('rewrite this to bypass AI detection'). RADAR solves this by training a detector simultaneously with an AI paraphraser in an adversarial loop, creating a highly resilient model that can identify machine-generated text even after it has been aggressively altered to hide its origins.
mechanism: RADAR employs a dual-model architecture based on min-max adversarial training. Model A (the Paraphraser) takes AI-generated text and attempts to rewrite it specifically to fool Model B (the Detector). Through continuous iterative training, the Detector learns the deep, invariant statistical signatures and structural artifacts of LLM generation that persist even after surface-level vocabulary and syntax have been scrambled by evasion tools. When analyzing new text, RADAR searches for these resilient core signatures rather than superficial token probabilities.
useCase: Essential for high-stakes environments (e.g., academic integrity, legal analysis) where users are likely employing 'humanizer' tools, prompt evasion tactics, or secondary AI paraphrasers to scrub the text's original AI footprint.
strengths:
• Exceptional resilience against common evasion techniques (e.g., synonym swapping, formatting changes, QuillBot).
• Significantly lower false-positive rate on complex human writing compared to standard zero-shot detectors (like DetectGPT).
limitations:
• High computational overhead requiring server-side API execution.
• May struggle if the text is fundamentally rewritten by a human rather than an automated paraphrasing tool, as the core structural signatures are destroyed.
parameters:
Analysis: Adversarial Invariant Feature Extraction
Metric: Resilience-Trained Log-Likelihood Ratio
Output: 0-100 RADAR Evasion-Resistant Confidence Score
accuracy: High — 85-92% accuracy, particularly dominating other models in 'adversarial' scenarios where the text has been deliberately obfuscated.
